knowledgePoint.zh: BERT的掩码语言建模——从两个方向理解语言
knowledgePoint.en: BERT's masked language modeling — understanding from both directions

recallIntro.zh: 你闭上眼，思绪飘回那个金色光芒中的开放空间。苏茨克维教授站在全息投影前，一段文本中有几个词被遮住了，显示为闪烁的空白。他用手指点了点其中一个空白处：「如果你只能从左边读，你会怎么猜这个词？现在，如果你能从两边同时看呢？」
recallIntro.en: You close your eyes, and your thoughts drift back to that open space bathed in golden light. Prof. Sutskever stands before a holographic projection where several words in a text passage are masked, showing as flickering blanks. He taps one of the blanks: 「If you could only read from the left, how would you guess this word? Now, what if you could look from both sides at once?」

recallOutro.zh: 你回过神来。两种阅读方式在脑海中并行——GPT从左到右，BERT从两个方向同时看。两条路各有所长，而它们的分歧与汇合，正在塑造一个新时代的轮廓。
recallOutro.en: You return to the present. Two reading paradigms run parallel in your mind — GPT reads left-to-right, BERT looks from both directions simultaneously. Each path has its strengths, and their divergence and convergence are shaping the outline of a new era.

text.zh: 金色的全息投影今天有了不同的模样。空中漂浮着一段很长的文本，但其中有几个词被替换成了闪烁的方块，像是被擦除了一样。苏茨克维教授走进来时，目光立刻被这些空白吸引。他端详了一会儿，然后转向你们。
text.en: The golden holographic projections look different today. A long passage of text floats in the air, but several words have been replaced by flickering squares — as if erased. When Prof. Sutskever walks in, his gaze is immediately drawn to these blanks. He studies them for a moment, then turns to you.

text.zh: 上节课我们讨论了GPT的思路，即从左到右预测下一个词。这是一种非常自然的方式，因为人类写作本身就是从左到右的。但我今天想介绍另一条路，一条由Google的团队在2018年10月提出的、与GPT截然不同的路。
text.en: Last lesson we discussed GPT's approach — predicting the next word from left to right. This is a very natural way, because human writing itself proceeds left to right. But today I want to introduce another path — one proposed by a team at Google in October 2018, fundamentally different from GPT.

text.zh: 这个方法叫{BERT}，全称是Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers，也就是来自Transformer的双向编码器表征。请注意这个关键词：双向。GPT是从左到右读的，它在预测第五个词的时候，只能看到前四个词。但BERT提出了一个不同的思路：为什么不能两边都看呢？
text.en: This method is called {BERT} — Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers. Notice the key word: bidirectional. GPT reads left to right — when predicting the fifth word, it can only see the first four words. But BERT asks: why not look from both sides?

text.zh: BERT的训练方法非常巧妙。它并非预测「下一个词」，而是随机将文本中百分之十五的词遮住，用一个特殊标记替换，然后让模型根据被遮住词左右两侧的上下文，来猜测原本的词是什么。这种方法被称为{掩码语言模型}。
text.en: BERT's training method is quite clever. Instead of predicting the 「next word, it randomly masks fifteen percent of the words in the text — replacing them with a special token — then asks the model to guess the masked word based on context from both the left and right sides. This is called a {masked language model}.

text.zh: 让我用一个例子来说明。假设原文是：「她买了一束玫瑰送给妈妈。」BERT会随机遮住其中一个词，变成：「她买了一束[MASK]送给妈妈。」现在，模型要猜这个[MASK]是什么。它可以看到左边的「一束」和右边的「送给妈妈」——两边的信息共同指向「玫瑰」或者「花」。这种双向的上下文，比只看左边强大得多。
text.en: Let me illustrate with an example. Suppose the original text is: 「She bought a bouquet of roses for her mother」. BERT randomly masks one word: 「She bought a bouquet of [MASK] for her mother」. Now the model must guess what [MASK] is. It can see 「a bouquet of」 on the left and 「for her mother」 on the right — information from both sides points to 「roses」 or 「flowers」. This bidirectional context is far more powerful than seeing only the left side.

text.zh: GPT从左到右预测下一个词，BERT遮住一个词然后从两边猜。这两种训练方式各有什么优势？
text.en: GPT predicts the next word left-to-right, while BERT masks a word and guesses from both sides. What are the advantages of each training approach?

text.zh: GPT更适合生成文本，毕竟写作本身就是从左到右的。而BERT更适合理解文本，因为它能同时看到两边的信息。
text.en: GPT is better for generating text — since writing itself is left-to-right; BERT is better for understanding text — since it can see both sides

text.zh: 这个分析非常精准。GPT的训练方式天然对齐了文本生成的过程，你就是在一个词一个词地往后写。因此，GPT可以流畅地生成长文本。而BERT因为能看到完整的上下文，在理解类任务上就占了优势，它能更准确地判断一段话的含义、两个句子的关系，或者一个词的准确语义。这两种设计哲学的分歧，将深刻影响整个领域的走向。
text.en: That analysis is very precise. GPT's training naturally aligns with the text generation process — you're writing one word after another. So GPT can fluently generate long text. BERT, because it can see the full context, has a natural advantage in understanding tasks — it can more accurately judge a passage's meaning, the relationship between two sentences, the precise semantics of a word. This divergence in design philosophy will profoundly influence the direction of the entire field.

text.zh: BERT获得的上下文信息更丰富——它每个位置都能看到完整句子，GPT只能看到部分
text.en: BERT gets richer context — each position can see the full sentence, while GPT only sees a partial one

text.zh: 你观察到了信息量的根本差异。在GPT中，第一个词的表征只基于它自己，第二个词只基于前两个词。但在BERT中，每一个词的表征都基于整个句子。这意味着BERT学到的每个词的内部表示都更加丰富和准确。这在需要精确理解的任务上优势明显，比如判断两句话是否矛盾、或者从文章中找到某个问题的答案。
text.en: You've observed the fundamental difference in information. In GPT, the first word's representation is based only on itself, the second word only on the first two words. But in BERT, every word's representation is based on the entire sentence. This means the internal representation BERT learns for each word is richer and more accurate. The advantage is clear in tasks requiring precise understanding — like determining whether two sentences contradict each other, or finding the answer to a question in a passage.

text.zh: GPT的训练目标更简单统一——它就是在做一件事：预测下一个词。BERT需要特殊的遮盖操作，有些不自然
text.en: GPT's training objective is simpler and more unified — it just does one thing: predict the next word. BERT needs special masking, which feels somewhat unnatural

text.zh: 你触及了一个微妙但重要的问题。GPT的优雅之处在于它的训练和使用完全一致——训练时预测下一个词，使用时也是生成下一个词。但BERT的训练和使用之间有一个裂缝：训练时有[MASK]标记，但实际使用时文本中没有这种标记。这种不匹配后来被证明确实带来了一些问题。有时候，最简单的方法反而是最好的方法。
text.en: You've touched on a subtle but important point. GPT's elegance lies in the perfect alignment between training and usage — during training it predicts the next word, during usage it generates the next word. But BERT has a gap between training and usage: [MASK] tokens appear during training but never during actual use. This mismatch was later shown to cause some problems. Sometimes the simplest approach turns out to be the best.

text.zh: 现在让我说说BERT在架构上的选择。GPT使用的是Transformer的解码器部分，只具备从左到右的注意力。而BERT使用的是Transformer的{编码器}部分，其注意力机制可以覆盖所有方向。这两种架构对应了两种不同的哲学。
text.en: Now let me discuss BERT's architectural choice. GPT uses the Transformer's decoder — with left-to-right attention only. BERT uses the Transformer's {encoder} — where attention can see in all directions. These two architectures correspond to two different philosophies.

text.zh: 解码器架构说：「我是一个作者，我一边写一边思考，只看已经写下的内容。」编码器架构说：「我是一个读者，我先读完整篇文章，然后才做出判断。」两种都有道理。但关键问题是：哪种方式能学到更深的语言理解？
text.en: The decoder architecture says: 「I'm a writer — I think as I write, only looking at what I've already written」. The encoder architecture says: 「I'm a reader — I read the entire article first, then make my judgment」. Both make sense. But the key question is: which approach learns deeper language understanding?

text.zh: BERT发表后的效果是惊人的。它在11个自然语言理解基准测试上全部取得了最好成绩，包括问答、文本蕴含、情感分析、语义相似度。在某些任务上，它甚至超过了人类的表现。整个NLP社区为之震动。
text.en: The results after BERT's publication were astonishing. It achieved the best scores on all 11 natural language understanding benchmarks — including question answering, textual entailment, sentiment analysis, and semantic similarity. On some tasks, it even surpassed human performance. The entire NLP community was shaken.

text.zh: BERT引发了一场「预训练竞赛」。Google之后，各大实验室纷纷推出自己的预训练模型——RoBERTa、ALBERT、XLNet、ELECTRA。每个模型都在BERT的基础上做出改进。一时间，不使用预训练模型做NLP研究变得几乎不可想象。预训练已经成为新的基础设施。
text.en: BERT triggered a 「pre-training race」. After Google, major labs released their own pre-trained models one after another — RoBERTa, ALBERT, XLNet, ELECTRA. Each improved upon BERT in some way. Suddenly, doing NLP research without pre-trained models became almost unthinkable. Pre-training had become the new infrastructure.

text.zh: BERT在理解类任务上大幅超越了之前的方法。你觉得为什么双向上下文对「理解」如此重要？
text.en: BERT dramatically surpassed previous methods on understanding tasks. Why do you think bidirectional context is so important for 「understanding」?

text.zh: 语言充满歧义——同一个词在不同上下文中意思完全不同，需要两边的信息才能确定
text.en: Language is full of ambiguity — the same word means different things in different contexts, requiring information from both sides to determine meaning

text.zh: 举一个经典的例子：「我去银行取了钱」和「我在河的北银行钓了鱼」——同样是「银行」这个词，在第一句中是金融机构，在第二句中是河岸。如果你只看到「我去银行」，你无法确定是哪个意思。但如果你同时看到后面的「取了钱」或者「钓了鱼」，意思就完全清楚了。双向上下文让BERT能做到这种精确的语义消歧。
text.en: Here's a classic example: 「I went to the bank to withdraw money」 versus 「I fished on the river bank」 — the same word 「bank」 means a financial institution in the first sentence and a riverside in the second. If you only see 「I went to the bank」, you can't be sure which meaning it is. But if you simultaneously see 「withdraw money」 or 「fished」 afterward, the meaning becomes perfectly clear. Bidirectional context lets BERT perform this kind of precise semantic disambiguation.

text.zh: 人类阅读时也是全局理解的——我们读完整段文字后才做出判断，而不是逐词做决定
text.en: Humans also understand globally when reading — we make judgments after reading the full passage, not word by word

text.zh: 这个类比很有启发性。你读一篇文章，不会读完第一个词就开始下结论。你会通读全文，让前后文互相印证，然后形成一个整体的理解。BERT的双向注意力某种程度上模拟了这种全局阅读的过程——每个词的表征都融合了整句话的信息。当然，人类阅读的机制远比这复杂，但方向是对的。
text.en: That analogy is very illuminating. When reading an article, you don't start drawing conclusions after the first word. You read through the whole text, letting preceding and following content corroborate each other, then form a holistic understanding. BERT's bidirectional attention in some sense simulates this process of global reading — each word's representation integrates information from the entire sentence. Of course, the mechanism of human reading is far more complex, but the direction is right.

text.zh: 双向信息让模型学到的词语表征更准确——每个词都携带了完整句子的信息
text.en: Bidirectional information lets the model learn more accurate word representations — each word carries information from the complete sentence

text.zh: 从表征学习的角度来说，这是核心优势。在GPT中，句子第一个词的表征只包含它自身的信息。但在BERT中，同一个词的表征融合了它左右所有词的信息。这意味着BERT生成的表征是「语境化的」——同一个词在不同句子中会有不同的表征。这种语境化表征在下游任务中表现极为出色。
text.en: From the representation learning perspective, this is the core advantage. In GPT, the first word's representation contains only its own information. But in BERT, the same word's representation integrates information from all words on both sides. This means BERT produces 「contextualized」 representations — the same word gets different representations in different sentences. These contextualized representations perform exceptionally well in downstream tasks.

text.zh: 但我要诚实地说——尽管BERT在理解任务上表现惊人，它有一个根本的局限性。BERT不能生成文本。它被训练来填空，不是来写作。你不能让BERT写一段故事或者回答一个开放性问题。在生成任务上，GPT的方法仍然是唯一的选择。
text.en: But I must be honest — despite BERT's amazing performance on understanding tasks, it has a fundamental limitation. BERT cannot generate text. It was trained to fill in blanks, not to write. You can't ask BERT to write a story or answer an open-ended question. For generation tasks, GPT's approach remains the only option.

text.zh: 到了2019年，NLP领域形成了两大阵营。一边是GPT阵营，采用解码器架构和单向注意力，擅长生成。另一边是BERT阵营，采用编码器架构和双向注意力，擅长理解。于是很多人开始思考：有没有可能把两者的优点结合起来？
text.en: By 2019, the NLP field had split into two camps. On one side, the GPT camp — decoder architecture, unidirectional attention, excelling at generation. On the other, the BERT camp — encoder architecture, bidirectional attention, excelling at understanding. Many were asking: is it possible to combine the strengths of both?

text.zh: 我的直觉是这样的：我相信最终答案在GPT的方向上。为什么？因为生成能力包含了理解能力。如果一个模型能写出完美的文章，它必然已经理解了语言。但反过来不一定成立，能理解不等于能创造。况且，GPT的训练目标更简单、更统一。我相信简洁的方法，如果配上足够的规模，会走得更远。
text.en: My intuition is this — I believe the ultimate answer lies in GPT's direction. Why? Because the ability to generate subsumes the ability to understand. If a model can write a perfect article, it must have already understood language. But the reverse doesn't necessarily hold — understanding doesn't equal creating. Moreover, GPT's training objective is simpler and more unified. I believe that a simpler method, given sufficient scale, will go further.

suggestedContent.zh: BERT（2018）的核心创新：掩码语言模型——随机遮住15%的词，让模型从双向上下文中猜测被遮住的词。使用Transformer编码器架构，实现双向注意力。在11个理解任务上取得最佳成绩。局限：无法生成文本。GPT与BERT代表了两种设计哲学：生成（单向解码器）vs 理解（双向编码器）。
suggestedContent.en: BERT (2018) core innovation: masked language model — randomly mask 15% of words, have the model guess masked words from bidirectional context. Uses Transformer encoder architecture for bidirectional attention. Achieved best results on 11 understanding tasks. Limitation: cannot generate text. GPT and BERT represent two design philosophies: generation (unidirectional decoder) vs understanding (bidirectional encoder).

text.zh: 苏茨克维教授认为GPT方向最终会胜出，因为「生成能力包含理解能力」。你同意这个判断吗？
text.en: Prof. Sutskever believes the GPT direction will ultimately prevail because 「the ability to generate subsumes understanding」. Do you agree with this judgment?

text.zh: 同意——如果你能完美地写出一段文字，你一定已经理解了它的内容
text.en: Agree — if you can perfectly write a passage, you must have already understood its content

text.zh: 这也是我的信念。想想看，如果一个模型能写出一篇准确的物理学论文，它必须理解物理学。如果它能写出一个合理的故事结局，它必须理解故事的情节和人物动机。生成是对理解的最严格检验。后来的发展确实印证了这一点，GPT-3和GPT-4在理解任务上的表现，甚至追上并超过了BERT系列模型。
text.en: That's my belief as well. Think about it — if a model can write an accurate physics paper, it must understand physics. If it can write a plausible story ending, it must understand the plot and character motivations. Generation is the strictest test of understanding. Later developments did confirm this — GPT-3 and GPT-4's performance on understanding tasks even caught up with or surpassed BERT-family models.

text.zh: 不一定——理解和生成可能是两种不同的能力，不能简单地说谁包含谁
text.en: Not necessarily — understanding and generation may be two different abilities, you can't simply say one subsumes the other

text.zh: 这是一个值得深思的反驳。确实有人能深刻地理解音乐，却不会作曲。也有人能写出流畅的文字，却对自己写的内容缺乏真正的理解。理解和生成之间的关系，可能比「包含」更复杂。但我仍然相信，在语言模型的语境中，足够强大的生成能力蕴含着深度的理解。这个信念是否正确，时间会告诉我们。
text.en: That's a counterargument worth deep reflection. Indeed, some people can profoundly understand music without being able to compose. Others can write fluent text without truly understanding what they've written. The relationship between understanding and generation may be more complex than 「subsumption」. But I still believe that in the context of language models, sufficiently powerful generation ability implies deep understanding. Whether this belief is correct — time will tell.

text.zh: 也许最终的方案需要结合两者——既有双向的理解，也有单向的生成
text.en: Perhaps the ultimate solution needs to combine both — bidirectional understanding and unidirectional generation

text.zh: （微微一笑）这是一种折中的智慧。事实上，后来确实出现了试图融合两者的架构，比如T5和UniLM。但有趣的是，到了GPT-3和GPT-4的时代，纯粹的解码器架构配上巨大的规模，在理解和生成两方面都达到了惊人的水平。也许融合不需要在架构层面发生——也许足够的规模本身就是最好的融合。
text.en: (Smiles slightly) That's a wisdom of compromise. In fact, architectures attempting to fuse both did appear later — like T5 and UniLM. But interestingly, by the era of GPT-3 and GPT-4, pure decoder architecture with enormous scale achieved astonishing levels in both understanding and generation. Perhaps fusion doesn't need to happen at the architectural level — perhaps sufficient scale itself is the best fusion.

text.zh: GPT和BERT的故事，本质上是两种理念的竞争：是选择简洁的单向生成，还是追求丰富的双向理解？但无论你站在哪一边，有一件事已经毫无疑问：预训练改变了一切。语言模型不再只是一种技术，它成为了NLP的基础。下节课，我们将看到一个更令人震撼的发现：当你把模型做得越来越大，会发生一些完全出乎意料的事情。
text.en: The story of GPT and BERT is essentially a competition between two philosophies — simple unidirectional generation, or rich bidirectional understanding? But regardless of which side you stand on, one thing is beyond doubt: pre-training changed everything. Language models are no longer just a technique — they've become the foundation of NLP. Next lesson, we'll see an even more astonishing discovery — when you make models larger and larger, something entirely unexpected happens.

suggestedContent.zh: 两大阵营：GPT（解码器，单向，擅长生成）vs BERT（编码器，双向，擅长理解）。BERT的掩码语言模型虽然在理解任务上表现出色，但无法生成文本。苏茨克维教授的信念：生成能力包含理解能力，因此GPT方向配合足够的规模将最终胜出。
suggestedContent.en: Two camps: GPT (decoder, unidirectional, excels at generation) vs BERT (encoder, bidirectional, excels at understanding). BERT's masked language model performs excellently on understanding tasks but cannot generate text. Sutskever's belief: generation ability subsumes understanding, so GPT's direction with sufficient scale will ultimately prevail.

text.zh: 苏茨克维教授走到全息投影前，轻轻用手指碰了碰那些闪烁的[MASK]方块。方块消失了，被遮住的词重新显现，句子恢复了完整。他注视着那段完整的文本，像是在思考什么。「两种阅读方式，两种理解世界的路径。」他低声说道。然后他转过身，目光投向远方。那个方向，金色的光芒更加浓烈，仿佛预示着规模所带来的更深层的变化正在等待你们。
text.en: Prof. Sutskever walks to the holographic projection and gently touches the flickering [MASK] blocks with his finger. The blocks disappear, the masked words reappear — the sentences are whole again. He gazes at the complete text, as if contemplating something. 「Two ways of reading, two paths to understanding the world, he murmurs. Then he turns, his gaze reaching far away — in that direction, the golden light grows more intense, as if heralding that deeper changes brought by scale await you.
